description: 3-2-5 (Teen Do Panch, also 2-3-5 or 5-3-2) is a trick-taking card game played in India, Pakistan, and Nepal. Three players use a 30-card deck. Each has a trick quota: dealer 2, player to dealer's right 5, player to dealer's left 3. The 5-trick player chooses trump and leads. Players above quota can 'pull' cards from those below in the next deal.

content.text: 3-2-5 (Teen Do Panch, also 2-3-5 or 5-3-2) is a trick-taking card game played in India, Pakistan, and Nepal. Three players use a 30-card deck. Each has a trick quota: dealer 2, player to dealer's right 5, player to dealer's left 3. The 5-trick player chooses trump and leads. Players above quota can 'pull' cards from those below in the next deal.
South Asia (India, Pakistan, Nepal). Closely related to Sergeant Major (3-5-8 / 8-5-3) played with 52 cards.
Exactly 3. Dealer has quota 2 tricks; player to dealer's right 5 tricks (chooses trump, leads); player to dealer's left 3 tricks.
30-card pack: remove 2s through 6s from 52, plus remove two 7s (usually keep 7♥ and 7♠). Rank A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7 high to low.
Three batches: 5 cards, then 3, then 2 to each player (10 each). Deal and play usually counter-clockwise.

items.text: Clockwise Deal and Play: Deal and play proceed clockwise instead of counter-clockwise, with the player to dealer's left taking the 5-trick quota, choosing trumps, and leading to the first trick while the player to dealer's right has the 3-trick quota.

Seventh Card Turned for Trump: Instead of freely announcing a trump suit, the 5-trick player may specify that the seventh card dealt to them (the middle card of the second batch of three) will be turned up and its suit becomes trumps.

Next Batch Highest Card Trump: Some play that the 5-trick player may choose trumps to be the suit of the highest card in the next batch of three cards dealt to them, or a randomly chosen card from the remainder of their hand.

Relaxed Return Suit Requirement: Instead of needing at least two remaining cards in the suit being returned after pulling, some play that a player who steals a card need only keep one card in that suit when choosing which card to give back.

Sevens as Permanent Trumps: In some circles both Sevens are permanent trumps: the 7 of hearts is the highest trump, followed by the 7 of spades, then the remaining cards of the chosen trump suit in their usual order.
Bonus for Winning All Ten Tricks: Some players award an extra 5 points, for a total of 15, to any player who succeeds in winning all ten tricks in a deal.

Trick Transfer and Loser Deals: Variants allow a below-quota player to transfer a trick to an above-quota player instead of giving up a card and may also make the biggest loser of a deal the next dealer instead of rotating the deal normally.
